implementation_notes: TypeScript's structural typing makes the replacement trivial: declare the operation as a free function over the target interface and the poltergeist disappears. The characteristic TS poltergeist is a factory returning `{ run() { /* ... */ } }` typed as an interface with one member, which forces every caller through an object it does not benefit from. Interfaces with a single member are also the smell's signature: an interface with one method and exactly one implementation is a function wearing a type.
idiom_name: factory returning a one-method object; interface it does not need
pitfalls: An interface with one method and one implementation is a function, and turning it into one removes the indirection entirely.
A DI token typed as a one-method interface is a common source of poltergeists in NestJS-style architectures.
A `class` with only a constructor argument and one method can usually be a factory function returning the dependency itself.
